bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw-material (copper and aluminium) cost volatility — Copper and aluminium are critical inputs forming an essential part of the cost base for consumer durables manufacturers. Copper prices rose to record levels during the year on AI data-centre and green-technology demand, while aluminium markets faced a structural supply shock; firms across the sector had to implement price increases in response to the escalation in key raw-material costs.
- Geopolitical conflict and energy-supply / supply-chain shock — The Middle East war disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and damaged production facilities in a region central to hydrocarbon supply, straining global supply chains, surging energy prices and raising the likelihood of a broader economic slowdown; escalating geopolitical tensions generated macroeconomic headwinds towards the close of the financial year.
- Trade protectionism and tariff regime uncertainty — The US imposed a minimum 10% tariff on many foreign goods with higher rates for India, and India faced an effective 50% export tariff on most merchandise goods to the US from August 6, 2025 before reduction to 10% in February 2026 - a volatile policy backdrop for trade flows and input sourcing.
- Climate change and decarbonization exposure (BRSR material issue) — Identified as a material risk: climate change exposes V-Guard to financial risk from regulations, emission targets, energy-cost volatility and investment in cleaner operations, while physical risks such as heat, water scarcity, floods and supply disruptions may affect operations and supply-chain resilience; decarbonization may cause unplanned cost increases from evolving environmental regulation.
- Water stress and water-management compliance (BRSR material issue) — Inadequate water management and rising water stress can disrupt operations, raise procurement/treatment/compliance costs and reduce efficiency; stricter regulation on water use and discharge creates compliance risk and penalties, while pollution or community impact could damage reputation and stakeholder trust.
- Demand seasonality and weather dependence — Seasonal variability shaped short-term sectoral performance dynamics, and demand conditions remained uneven across parts of the consumer durables sector - a structural exposure for a portfolio weighted to weather-linked categories.
- Regulatory change in energy-efficiency and tax norms — The Bureau of Energy Efficiency revised mandatory star labelling for a broad range of appliances effective January 1, 2026, tightening efficiency standards and making high-star-rated products more expensive; GST 2.0 effective September 22, 2025 reset appliance tax rates - both reshape product cost, pricing and portfolio economics.
- New Labour Codes raising employee-benefit obligations — Pursuant to the new Labour Codes notified in November 2025, an incremental charge towards gratuity and leave encashment provisions was recognised as an exceptional item, and management attributed the year's decline in Return on Net Worth largely to it - a recurring cost-base risk from labour regulation.

outlook.body:
- Maintain a deliberately diversified business model across consumer electricals, electronics and durables so the portfolio can absorb cyclical and seasonal shocks while participating in multiple growth categories
- Keep expanding the geographic footprint beyond South India - nearly half of revenues now come from non-South markets - on a distribution base of over 1,00,000 retail touchpoints
- Scale backward integration and in-house manufacturing, which now accounts for nearly 65% of the portfolio, with capacity expansion initiatives progressing across Batteries, Fans and Modular Switches
- Deepen backward integration in battery manufacturing under VCPL (Pantnagar inverters, Hyderabad batteries) to strengthen supply-chain control, cost efficiency and category margins
- Build a position in next-generation energy storage through the associate stake in Gegadyne Energy Labs, raised to 30.35% on a fully diluted basis in March 2026
- Enter the Lighting category to bridge a white space in the Electricals portfolio, launching first through an outsourced model in the Company's stronger southern markets and scaling investment to market response
- Grow Switches and Switchgears as a natural adjacency to the core Wires business, leveraging the Simon Electric acquisition and the Simon Global brand licence and technology collaboration, plus GUTS Electro-Mech for MCBs/RCCBs
- Prioritise leadership in the mid-market premium and BLDC fan segments rather than the economy segment, through investment in technology, innovation, design and in-house manufacturing
- Merge wholly-owned subsidiary Sunflame Enterprises Pvt. Ltd. into V-Guard (Board in-principle approval, July 2025) to accelerate synergies across sourcing, R&D, product development and go-to-market
- Strengthen in-house technology, design and product development through the Innovation Campus inaugurated in January 2026, sustaining a design-led approach recognised by the Red Dot Award and German Design Award
- Run the business with disciplined inventory management, calibrated pricing actions and agile market execution through input-cost and demand volatility
- Advance digitisation across marketing and go-to-market operations, and the Saksham HR transformation programme, alongside sharpened Vision and Mission statements
- Anchor growth in a defined ESG framework, including structured engagement with critical and strategic suppliers and community programmes through the V-Guard Foundation
- Dividend is governed by a formal Dividend Distribution Policy framed under Regulation 43A of the SEBI Listing Regulations and disclosed in the annual report and on the Company's website. The policy's stated intent is that a company may distribute all of its profits or distribute a certain percentage and retain the balance in the business for purposes such as expansion, diversification and inorganic investments, and that a formal policy helps the Board arrive at a balanced dividend pay-out ratio taking into account the profit made during the relevant financial year, expansion programmes and other strategic plans. For FY 2025-26 the Board recommended a final dividend of Rs 1.50 per equity share, placed before members at the 30th AGM.
- Structured materiality assessment covering global megatrends, regulatory developments, ESG standards and stakeholder expectations identified 21 material ESG topics, reviewed and approved by the Board of Directors and integrated, with associated ESG risks, into the Enterprise Risk Management framework
- Initiated a double materiality assessment during the year to further enhance sustainability governance and reporting
- Decarbonization strategy advanced through renewable-energy adoption, energy efficiency, product life-cycle assessments (LCAs) and TCFD-aligned climate risk assessments across scenarios, with expanding renewable capacity and climate risks integrated into the ERM framework
- Water stewardship: reducing freshwater dependency through conservation, rainwater harvesting, recycling and reuse; enhanced STP/ETP systems with added ultra-filtration; IoT-based monitoring for real-time tracking, compliance and efficiency; community-driven water conservation initiatives
- Sustainability-focused product portfolio positioned as a growth opportunity, with lower-carbon operations expected to support cost savings, energy-cost resilience and new market access
- Limited assurance on BRSR core and select BRSR indicators obtained from Price Waterhouse Chartered Accountants LLP, covering the employee/worker, diversity and turnover disclosures
- Customer grievance performance: about 95% of customer complaints, covering product issues within and beyond the warranty period, are resolved within 48 hours, under a documented grievance redressal mechanism available to every stakeholder group
- Stakeholder Engagement Policy published on the Company website as the grievance-redressal mechanism for investors, communities, shareholders, employees, workers and value-chain partners
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: V-Guard's expansion is centred on deepening in-house manufacturing rather than greenfield scale. In Electronics, the Company continued to scale up backward integration in battery manufacturing: alongside the inverter manufacturing facility at VCPL Pantnagar, a battery plant was established under VCPL on the outskirts of Hyderabad and became operational at the end of FY24, with in-house capacity now contributing about 50% of total category sales and improving category margins. In May 2025 the Company initiated a strategic capacity expansion at that Hyderabad battery facility which will more than double existing capacity, involving an investment of about Rs 50 Crore and targeted for completion within 18 months, driven by anticipated growth in the domestic battery storage market and expected to improve margins through in-house manufacturing efficiencies and scale. Technology capacity is being added inorganically as well: in March 2026 the Company invested a further Rs 25 Crore in Mumbai-based deep-technology firm Gegadyne Energy Labs Pvt. Ltd., taking its holding to 30.35% on a fully diluted basis, to access next-generation battery cell, pack and rack systems; Gegadyne has moved from prototype to pilot and is transitioning from pilot production to commercialisation with limited-scale proof-of-concept supplies. In Electricals, the Wires business runs a fully integrated, 100% in-house manufacturing model with facilities at Coimbatore and Kashipur; the modular switches platform rests on the FY23 acquisition and integration of Simon Electric Pvt. Ltd., whose manufacturing unit at Haridwar, Uttarakhand is paired with a brand licence and technology collaboration with Simon Global; and switchgear capability was strengthened by acquiring 100% of Hyderabad-based GUTS Electro-Mech Ltd., which makes MCBs and RCCBs. The Company also announced a foray into the Lighting business in FY26, to be launched initially through an outsourced model aimed at consumer and residential markets in its stronger southern markets, with future investment scaled according to market response and operational needs. Distribution capacity spans a network of over 1,00,000 retail touchpoints, with nearly half of revenues now coming from non-South markets.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Stabilizers: near-term demand subdued on a weak summer and soft air-conditioner sales, but the category retains structural support from rising penetration of high-value appliances and the need for voltage protection, supporting gradual medium-term recovery and penetration in newly electrified rural and upcountry markets
- Digital UPS (inverters and batteries): structurally linked to recurring electricity shortages, giving steady demand visibility; described as one of the most resilient and scalable growth engines in Electronics
- The GST reduction on lead-acid batteries from 28% to 18% has improved affordability and supported demand
- In-house battery capacity at the Hyderabad facility now contributes about 50% of category sales, with the resulting efficiencies translating into better category margins
- Solar Power Systems: rooftop inverter and panel business scaling fast on rising residential and commercial rooftop adoption, favourable policy incentives and the energy-transition trend; the GST cut from 12% to 5% is expected to further improve demand, though the category stays price-competitive and externally influenced
- Wires: demand driven by electrification trends and real estate expansion, roughly 90-95% of sales from retail trade, performance closely tied to copper prices with dynamic pass-through pricing in both directions
- Electricals overall is linked to construction activity, real estate growth, seasonal weather, water-table levels and consumer spending; recent growth has come from pricing actions, commodity tailwinds, new products and adjacency expansion
- Pumps: inherently seasonal and rural-skewed - demand rises as summer water tables fall and softens in heavy monsoon; purchase decisions are influenced by retailers and plumbers, making channel relationships important
- Fans: new BEE energy-rating norms effective January 1, 2026 and sharp copper inflation are accelerating the structural shift to BLDC fans, which now account for a significant portion of fan sales; adoption in rural/upcountry markets remains constrained by volatile voltage affecting electronic controllers, and elevated industry inventory is expected to normalise gradually
- Air Coolers: FY26 hurt by an early monsoon and unusually mild summer in Southern and Eastern markets; management expects a strong rebound in demand supported by a low base and normalisation of seasonal conditions, along with continued product innovation and design upgrades
- Water Heaters: relatively resilient, supported by new launches such as the Luxecube smart water heater range; seasonally influenced with upside from colder weather, and highly competitive with 20-30 active brands requiring sustained innovation and product refresh
- Kitchen Appliances: consumption headwinds in line with FMCG trends, with induction cooktops gaining momentum late in the year aided by LPG availability constraints; institutional channels such as CSD remain under pressure while general and modern trade show better traction, and water purifiers scale via e-commerce with phased entry into organised retail
- Sunflame: segment margins improved to 5.3% from 2.5% on early integration benefits - stronger cost structures, better service levels and faster resolution metrics - with salesforce and distribution integration nearing completion
- Long-term Indian consumer-durables demand supported by rising incomes, increasing electrification, urbanisation, deeper Tier II and Tier III penetration, energy efficiency, smart connectivity and rapid product innovation
- Operating environment marked by input-cost volatility, tariff-related uncertainty and geopolitical effects on supply chains and market sentiment; FY26 was a year of contrasting halves with a weak first-half summer and improved second-half momentum

business_model.body: V-Guard Industries Limited (incorporated February 12, 1996) manufactures and sells household and small-commercial electrical and electronic products across three activity groups - Electronics (stabilizers, digital UPS and solar power systems), Electrical (PVC insulated cables, switchgears, pumps and modular switches) and Consumer Durables (electric and solar water heaters, fans and kitchen appliances). Products are sold pan-India through distributive trade (dealers, distributors and direct marketing associates), modern trade and regional specialty chains, e-commerce/quick commerce, Central Police Canteens, Canteen Stores Department and institutions. The consolidated business also includes the wholly-owned subsidiaries GUTS Electro-Mech Ltd., V-Guard Consumer Products Ltd. and Sunflame Enterprises Pvt. Ltd., and associate Gegadyne Energy Labs Pvt. Ltd.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Stabilizers: near-term demand subdued on a weak summer and soft air-conditioner sales, but the category retains structural support from rising penetration of high-value appliances and the need for voltage protection, supporting gradual medium-term recovery and penetration in newly electrified rural and upcountry markets
- Digital UPS (inverters and batteries): structurally linked to recurring electricity shortages, giving steady demand visibility; described as one of the most resilient and scalable growth engines in Electronics
- The GST reduction on lead-acid batteries from 28% to 18% has improved affordability and supported demand
- In-house battery capacity at the Hyderabad facility now contributes about 50% of category sales, with the resulting efficiencies translating into better category margins
- Solar Power Systems: rooftop inverter and panel business scaling fast on rising residential and commercial rooftop adoption, favourable policy incentives and the energy-transition trend; the GST cut from 12% to 5% is expected to further improve demand, though the category stays price-competitive and externally influenced
- Wires: demand driven by electrification trends and real estate expansion, roughly 90-95% of sales from retail trade, performance closely tied to copper prices with dynamic pass-through pricing in both directions
- Electricals overall is linked to construction activity, real estate growth, seasonal weather, water-table levels and consumer spending; recent growth has come from pricing actions, commodity tailwinds, new products and adjacency expansion
- Pumps: inherently seasonal and rural-skewed - demand rises as summer water tables fall and softens in heavy monsoon; purchase decisions are influenced by retailers and plumbers, making channel relationships important
- Fans: new BEE energy-rating norms effective January 1, 2026 and sharp copper inflation are accelerating the structural shift to BLDC fans, which now account for a significant portion of fan sales; adoption in rural/upcountry markets remains constrained by volatile voltage affecting electronic controllers, and elevated industry inventory is expected to normalise gradually
- Air Coolers: FY26 hurt by an early monsoon and unusually mild summer in Southern and Eastern markets; management expects a strong rebound in demand supported by a low base and normalisation of seasonal conditions, along with continued product innovation and design upgrades
- Water Heaters: relatively resilient, supported by new launches such as the Luxecube smart water heater range; seasonally influenced with upside from colder weather, and highly competitive with 20-30 active brands requiring sustained innovation and product refresh
- Kitchen Appliances: consumption headwinds in line with FMCG trends, with induction cooktops gaining momentum late in the year aided by LPG availability constraints; institutional channels such as CSD remain under pressure while general and modern trade show better traction, and water purifiers scale via e-commerce with phased entry into organised retail
- Sunflame: segment margins improved to 5.3% from 2.5% on early integration benefits - stronger cost structures, better service levels and faster resolution metrics - with salesforce and distribution integration nearing completion
- Long-term Indian consumer-durables demand supported by rising incomes, increasing electrification, urbanisation, deeper Tier II and Tier III penetration, energy efficiency, smart connectivity and rapid product innovation
- Operating environment marked by input-cost volatility, tariff-related uncertainty and geopolitical effects on supply chains and market sentiment; FY26 was a year of contrasting halves with a weak first-half summer and improved second-half momentum

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: V-Guard's expansion is centred on deepening in-house manufacturing rather than greenfield scale. In Electronics, the Company continued to scale up backward integration in battery manufacturing: alongside the inverter manufacturing facility at VCPL Pantnagar, a battery plant was established under VCPL on the outskirts of Hyderabad and became operational at the end of FY24, with in-house capacity now contributing about 50% of total category sales and improving category margins. In May 2025 the Company initiated a strategic capacity expansion at that Hyderabad battery facility which will more than double existing capacity, involving an investment of about Rs 50 Crore and targeted for completion within 18 months, driven by anticipated growth in the domestic battery storage market and expected to improve margins through in-house manufacturing efficiencies and scale. Technology capacity is being added inorganically as well: in March 2026 the Company invested a further Rs 25 Crore in Mumbai-based deep-technology firm Gegadyne Energy Labs Pvt. Ltd., taking its holding to 30.35% on a fully diluted basis, to access next-generation battery cell, pack and rack systems; Gegadyne has moved from prototype to pilot and is transitioning from pilot production to commercialisation with limited-scale proof-of-concept supplies. In Electricals, the Wires business runs a fully integrated, 100% in-house manufacturing model with facilities at Coimbatore and Kashipur; the modular switches platform rests on the FY23 acquisition and integration of Simon Electric Pvt. Ltd., whose manufacturing unit at Haridwar, Uttarakhand is paired with a brand licence and technology collaboration with Simon Global; and switchgear capability was strengthened by acquiring 100% of Hyderabad-based GUTS Electro-Mech Ltd., which makes MCBs and RCCBs. The Company also announced a foray into the Lighting business in FY26, to be launched initially through an outsourced model aimed at consumer and residential markets in its stronger southern markets, with future investment scaled according to market response and operational needs. Distribution capacity spans a network of over 1,00,000 retail touchpoints, with nearly half of revenues now coming from non-South markets.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Diversified three-pillar portfolio - Electrical (~43% of turnover), Electronics (~29%) and Consumer Durables (~28%) - reducing dependence on any single category
- Pan-India manufacturing and distribution footprint: 9 manufacturing facilities, 34 warehouses/hubs and 31 branch offices, all with operational and financial control
- Steadily expanding presence outside South India, with the non-South share of revenue rising over FY21-FY26 to roughly half of the mix
- Multi-channel reach spanning distributive trade, modern trade, e-commerce/quick commerce, canteen/institutional channels
- In-house R&D Innovation Centre and a dedicated lab supporting product development
- Group structure adds owned manufacturing and category depth through wholly-owned subsidiaries GUTS Electro-Mech, V-Guard Consumer Products and Sunflame Enterprises, plus a 30.35% associate stake in battery-technology firm Gegadyne Energy Labs
- Established customer-grievance infrastructure handling a very large complaint volume with a stated grievance redressal mechanism in place for every stakeholder group

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: West Asia conflict driving raw material shortages (aluminum, polymers, sulfuric acid); prolonged inflationary pressure; channel inventory imbalances in non-South; new entrants in Wires and Fans; monsoon variability impacting demand

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Channel financing covers 35% of business (distributor-level, not category-specific); TPW fan shortages due to plastic resin scarcity, not demand; BLDC in mixer grinders not viable due to low usage hours; Kerala remittances show no material impact yet; solar growth is B2C-focused to preserve pricing power

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Maintain a deliberately diversified business model across consumer electricals, electronics and durables so the portfolio can absorb cyclical and seasonal shocks while participating in multiple growth categories
- Keep expanding the geographic footprint beyond South India - nearly half of revenues now come from non-South markets - on a distribution base of over 1,00,000 retail touchpoints
- Scale backward integration and in-house manufacturing, which now accounts for nearly 65% of the portfolio, with capacity expansion initiatives progressing across Batteries, Fans and Modular Switches
